newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC wants quick resumption of EU wheat exports.
newsitem.headline: ONIC wants quick resumption of EU wheat exports.

text.p: France's ONIC cereals office, disappointed by a new tax on European Union wheat exports, on Wednesday urged a quick start to the next annual campaign due to start officially on July 1.

Director general Alain Moulinier told reporters he regretted Wednesday's Commission decision to reimpose a 15 Ecu ($20) per tonne standing tax on exports but said this ought not to stand in the way of early marketing of the next crop.
"We firmly believe the Commission should start up the (next) campaign quickly," he told a news conference.
The Brussels-based executive proposed the tax in April but had to wait until today to see it agreed by its 20 commissioners after French member Edith Cresson blocked the plan last week.
Moulinier denied press suggestions linking Cresson's move to French parliamentary elections or purely national interests, saying she had acted independently.
The Commission has meanwhile blocked new wheat exports for the current campaign after reaching its export target and seeing a rise in demand and prices for grain inside the EU.

Moulinier said he was advising the French government to argue for an early resumption of exports in regular grain talks with Brussels. The EU should take a lead on world markets rather than acting restrictively towards wheat sales, he said.
He added commercial exporters would need a signal from the EU it was ready to respond quickly to demand when necessary.
He cited a Tunisian tender to buy 125,000 tonnes of wheat between July and September, which traders later said had been awarded at prices from $173.42 to $176.50 a tonne with freight.
The tender makes room for wheat to be supplied from the EU, United States or Canada but traders said the EU was most likely.
